title: Activepieces vs Node-RED: Which Tool Wins in 2026?
summary: Activepieces vs Node-RED: choose based on your team's JavaScript skills and whether you need to automate devices or business apps.
body_markdown:
## Device and business app connections


Some things emit signals, and some are things people type into. Node-RED connects to the first, like sensors, controllers and message brokers. Business-app tools connect to the second, like CRMs, ticketing and inboxes.


Out of the box, Node-RED ships MQTT, TCP, UDP, HTTP and WebSocket nodes in its core. Serial-port and Modbus support come as installable nodes, the Modbus ones from community packages.


A flow that polls a Modbus register every second and publishes to an MQTT broker is therefore a handful of wired nodes. In a business-app tool, the same job means standing up a bridge service first.


Community nodes are volunteer-maintained, so check a node's last update before you build a production line on it.


### SaaS apps and business systems


For CRMs, ticketing, email and chat apps, the pre-built catalogue's what lets a mixed team build without a developer.


The[Activepieces GitHub monorepo](https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces/tree/main/packages/pieces/community) shows the count rising from 100 integrations in 2023 to 280+ by March 2025, which means teams can automate workflows across far more of their existing tools without custom development.


It passed 600+ by the end of 2025 and **reached 746 in 2026** .


What matters is pace: the app your company adopts next year is more likely to be covered already, and each gap closed is one fewer set of hand-written API calls for someone to maintain.


*(chart)*


That pace only matters for the apps you actually run, and the next question is who wires them up.


In Activepieces, someone in operations describes the process in the built-in chat, say an approval that touches the CRM and the billing system, and the chat builds and publishes it as a live flow in your account, identical to what a developer would have assembled by hand.


That flow answers to the same RBAC and audit logs as every other, and each run leaves a trace anyone on the team can open and read, no developer needed to interpret it. MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production.


You don't hire for this, you describe it; Node-RED stays the answer for the Modbus line.


### Why connector counts mislead in comparisons


Compare the counts and you're not comparing like with like. One side tallies packaged app integrations. The other includes protocol primitives and community-contributed nodes, which vary widely in depth and upkeep. A bigger number doesn't tell you whether your ten systems are covered.


List those ten systems and check each one against both catalogues. Where a connector is missing, a generic HTTP request step works in either tool.


But you then own authentication, pagination and error handling yourself. It lands on whoever built the workflow, and it's the reason the next criterion is about who that person is.
